slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you
naturally easy to open up to
Asking how someone is, then waiting for the real answer. "No, really, how are you?" A second question shows you actually want to know.
Not rushing to give advice. Let people finish and ask if they want your opinion. Most people just want to feel heard first. Advice can wait.
Keeping what people tell you private. Once you're known as someone who never repeats things, people start trusting you with what matters.
Sharing your own struggles sometimes. "I've had a rough month too." A little vulnerability tells people it's safe to be honest with you.
Bringing calm into conversations. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a steadier mind makes me a better listener when it counts.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A steadier mind makes me a better listener when it counts.

slides.texte_overlay: Reacting kindly to bad news. No "I told you so," no lecture. A gentle reaction teaches people they can come to you when things go wrong.
Checking in a few days later. "How did it go with your dad?" Remembering and following up shows people their problems matter to you.
